noveltyJustification: First iteration; all findings are new to this lineage and establish the rule inventory, severity map, and empirically probed detectability gaps.

ruledOut: Re-deriving the eight confirmed starting facts
Flipping every warn rule to error irrespective of failure class

summary: evaluate() maps severity 'block'|'error' to blocking and everything else (including missing severity) to advisory warn; a warn rule can never deny a dispatch.
Full inventory: 23 rule declarations across seven cli-* skills, 7 declared error and 16 warn; cli-claude-code (2 warn) and cli-opencode (5 warn) declare no error rule.

Zero-error posture for cli-claude-code and cli-opencode is an oversight in both: each contains at least one rule whose violation is a silent hang or silent wrong result, and claude-code's peers' availability rules are simply absent rather than deliberately omitted.

stdin-redirect-required is the highest-value severity flip: seven identical warn declarations, one deterministic check that covers every headless shape and passes on redirect/heredoc/herestring/pipe; violation hangs with zero output indistinguishable from a slow model.

Empirical probes confirm silent passes for: hermes chat without a query flag, --agent=general, --share=public, unquoted slash prompts, -t search,todo (no file), -s preload exemption, and -t shell without --yolo; each is a detectability gap in a declared check.

Availability coverage is inconsistent: five skills declare availability at error (codex, cursor, devin, hermes, pi) while claude-code and opencode declare none and the registry implements no command-v-claude-required / command-v-opencode-required.
The dispatch README documents five registered checks while CHECKS exports 17 — a severity audit performed from the README would be wrong.
